title: Service failure containment and recovery procedure
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook documents a standard operating procedure for containing an active service failure, stabilizing customer-facing traffic, and executing a prioritized recovery while protecting SLOs and stewarding error budget. It is intended for SREs on pager duty, incident commanders, and service owners.

Goals
-----
- Contain blast radius within 5 minutes of detection for tier-1 customer-facing services.
- Restore critical SLOs (availability P99/weekly, latency P95) to within acceptable error budget consumption within 2 hours when feasible.
- Leave clear handoff artifacts for a post-incident review and capacity reconciliation.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
This procedure applies to Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, routing and model-serving control planes, and related tenant-facing proxies. It does NOT substitute process for long-running mitigations (capacity upgrades, model rollbacks that require change approvals). For private deployments, follow the customer-specific escalation in eng-private-deployments/* pages.

Key definitions and SLO priorities
----------------------------------
- Critical SLOs: Availability (user-facing request success rate) and Latency P95 for interactive generation.
- Secondary SLOs: Embedding throughput, batch job completion windows, and background metrics (indexing/replication).
- Error budget: 28-day rolling window for availability; threshold for emergency actions is >= 50% budget consumed.

SLO priority matrix (quick reference)
-------------------------------------
| Priority | SLO name                | Emergency action when breached |
|----------|-------------------------|-------------------------------|
| P0       | API availability (prod) | Immediate throttling, global fallback to low-cost model variant |
| P1       | Latency P95 (prod)      | Selective tenant rate-limiting, degrade caching TTLs |
| P2       | Embeddings throughput   | Defer background jobs, queue backfill |

Ownership and communications
----------------------------
- Incident commander (IC): first responder on page. Uses PagerDuty escalation policy.
- Service owner: notified within 10 minutes for P0 or P1 incidents.
- Communication channels: #oncall (Slack), "Incident <service>-YYYYMMDD" Zoom bridge, status.redwood.internal for external customer status when required.

Detection and initial assessment (0–5 minutes)
-----------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge the page and create an incident in the incident tracker (set severity based on SLO impact).
2. Capture the following immediately in the incident timeline: triggered alert, metric values, affected regions, and tenant impact sample.
3. Quick triage: classify as (a) traffic surge, (b) model-serving regression, (c) infra failure, (d) external dependency.
4. If classification uncertain after 3 minutes, assume a traffic surge and apply protective throttles (see mitigation step 2).

Containment and mitigation actions (5–30 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------
Follow these ordered actions. Stop when the service shows stabilization signals (error rate < SLO threshold for 5 consecutive minutes) and IC confirms.

Primary containment steps (ordered)
1. Short-circuit noncritical paths: disable telemetry sampling or metrics that cause backpressure.
2. Apply traffic shaping via the Traffic Shaper service: reduce inbound rate to the service by 25% increments until error rate improves. Priority: apply tenant-level fairshare first, then global limits.
   - CLI example: rctl traffic-shaper set --service inference-prod --mode fairshare --percent 75
3. Set model fallback policy in routing: switch a portion (10–50%) of requests to a compatible lower-resource model variant to reduce memory/KV pressure.
   - Routing JSON example: {"route_policy":"fallback","target":"gpt-lite-v1","percent":30}
4. If memory OOMs are observed across nodes, trigger immediate pod eviction protection and increase instance replacement parallelism to 5 to avoid cascading restarts.
   - kubectl annotate deployment/inference-serving redwood/restart-parallelism=5 --overwrite

Capacity triage and temporary provisioning (30–90 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Inspect autoscaler signals and queue length. If autoscaler is throttled by budget, request emergency capacity grant from Capacity Escrow (steps below).
2. Emergency capacity grant procedure (fast path):
   - IC opens Capacity Escrow ticket with SLA justification and estimated delta (GPUs or CPU nodes).
   - If approved, call Capacity API to add nodes in the hot-pool: capacity-cli add --pool inference-hot --nodes 4 --reason "P0 containment"
3. Rebalance tenants: if multi-tenant contention detected, migrate low-priority tenants to degraded mode using the tenant-evict tool. Record tenant IDs and reasons.

Error budget stewardship and SLO reconciliation
----------------------------------------------
- If error budget consumption will exceed the emergency cutoff (>=50%), trigger SLO-driven mitigation: reduce noncritical quotas, pause experimental routes, and extend model TTL caching aggressively.
- Document every error-budget-consuming action in the incident timeline with rationale and owner.
- Post-recovery, schedule a 2-business-day SLO reconciliation to decide remedial engineering actions and possible customer SLAs.

Operational tooling and telemetry checklist
----------------------------------------
- Observability: confirm the following dashboards are visible and updated: API availability, P95 latency by route, KV cache hit ratio, model memory pressure, per-tenant QPS.
- Tracing: check top 20 traces by execution time for new latencies.
- Logging: attach representative error logs (sampling 1%) and set retention for the incident window.

Communication and customer-facing posture
----------------------------------------
1. IC drafts a short incident summary for the internal channel within 15 minutes: impact, actions taken, next steps.
2. If outage meets customer-impact thresholds or 15+ customers affected, prepare a status page update and route to Customer Success for approval.
3. Use the status template: impact, affected regions/tenants, mitigation in progress, ETA for next update.

Handover and recovery to steady-state (90–240 minutes)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Verify SLO metrics have returned to normal for 30 consecutive minutes under the adjusted traffic profile.
2. Gradually roll back temporary throttles and fallback routes in reverse order of application, monitoring a 5-minute rolling window after each rollback.
3. If capacity was added from the hot-pool, begin a planned shrink: capacity-cli remove --pool inference-hot --nodes 4 --grace 30m --reason "post-incident"
4. Prepare a handoff doc for the on-call rotation: cause hypothesis, mitigations applied, outstanding remediation, and next-priority tickets.

Post-incident review and remediation (within 7 days)
---------------------------------------------------
1. Within 48 hours: IC and service owner produce a one-page timeline and evidence bundle.
2. Within 7 days: hold a blameless post-incident review with SRE, service, and product stakeholders. Include:
   - Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
   - SLO impact and exact error budget consumption.
   - Remediation plan with owners and target dates.
3. Required remediation examples: model rollback/patch, autoscaler tuning, code-level memory fix, capacity commitments, improved observability panels.

Operational runbook snippets and configs
---------------------------------------
- Traffic-shaper example YAML:
  apiVersion: redwood/v1
  kind: TrafficShaperPolicy
  metadata:
    name: inference-emergency-throttle
  spec:
    mode: fairshare
    maxPercent: 75
    tenantOverrides:
      - tenant: prod-customer-a
        percent: 40

- Autoscaler quick check (CLI):
  autoscaler-cli status --service inference-prod --quiet

Escalation matrix and decision thresholds
----------------------------------------
- Escalate to Platform Manager after 60 minutes of P0 impact without meaningful recovery progress.
- Escalate to CTO and Customer Success for any incident that affects >= 250 customers or causes >= 2 hours of major outage.

Metrics to capture for the retro
-------------------------------
- Time to acknowledge, time to first mitigation, time to stabilization, capacity delta applied, error budget delta, number of tenants evicted, number of rollbacks initiated.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge page and create incident.
2. Classify incident type and capture affected tenants.
3. Apply traffic-shaper fairshare at 75%.
4. Enable model fallback 30% to gpt-lite-v1.
5. Inspect autoscaler; request emergency capacity if queue length > 1000 and scale suppressed.
6. Notify service owner and Customer Success if > 15 customers affected.
7. Document all error-budget actions in timeline.
8. Begin handoff once stabilized for 30 minutes.
